sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Dhirendra Kumar Srivastava

Counsel for Opposite Party :- Ashutosh Kumar Pandey,G.A.
Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.

1. Heard Sri Dhirendra Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Ashutosh Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and Sri Pankaj Srivastava, learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. The instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking quashing of the entire criminal proceedings of Complaint Case No. 76 of 2019 under Section 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C.
and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Mahila Thana, District-Chandauli as well as summoning order dated 29.04.2019.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the instant proceedings were arising out of the matrimonial dispute between the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no.2 and vide order dated 6.8.2019, the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the parties have settled their disputes amicably before the Mediation Centre and a final settlement dated 7.10.2020 was arrived at between the parties.

Accordingly, the parties have filed an Application under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, which was allowed and the entire payment has already been paid to the opposite party no.2 by the applicant.
Therefore, learned counsel for the applicant seeks quashing of the entire proceedings of the instant case on the basis of the settlement arrived at between the parties.
4. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 does not dispute the aforesaid facts and has admitted the receipt of the entire payment in terms of the settlement.
5. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties in the mediation centre, learned A.G.A. do not oppose the prayer for quashing of the instant complaint case.
6. Having heard the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court has carefully gone through the record of the case.

7. From the record of the case, it is apparent that there was matrimonial dispute between the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no.2 and vide order dated 6.8.2019, the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre, where the parties have amicably settled the dispute in terms of settlement agreement dated 07.10.2020, which reads as under:-
"a) That the parties have settled their dispute and decided take mutually divorce and in this regard they have filed a petition u/s 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act before the Family Court, Chandauli which is registered as Petition No. 112 of 2020.
The certified copy of aforesaid divorce petition is being annexed to this settlement-agreement for kind perusal of the Hon'ble Court.
b) That the parties have settled their dispute on the condition that the applicant-husband shall pay a permanent alimony including Stridhan of

Rs.
03,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs only) to the wife Pooja Kumari

. 
c) That demand draft bearing no. 492546 dated 03.10.2020 for Rs. 1,50,000/- drawn on State Bank of India in favour of wife namely Pooja Kumari and which has been handed over to the wife i.e. O.P. No. 2 today i.e. 07.10.2020 by the applicant-husband and she has acknowledged the receipt of the same.
d) That the remaining amount i.e. Rs. 1,50,000/- shall be paid by the husband to the wife through demand draft at the time of final decree of the mutual divorce petition in Family Court, Chandauli.

8. In view of the aforesaid settlement, the parties had filed the application under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, which has been allowed and the marriage has been dissolved.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the entire payment has been made to the opposite party no. 2 in view of the settlement.
In view thereof, no fruitful purpose would be served in keeping the proceedings pending against the applicants.

9. Having regard to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, since the parties have already settled all their disputes amicably, therefore, the instant application is allowed in terms of the settlement dated 07.10.2020, the entire proceedings of the Complaint Case No. 76 of 2019 under Section 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Mahila Thana,
District-Chandauli as well as summoning order dated 29.04.2019 are hereby quashed in the light of the judgements of the Apex Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and Another : (2012) 10 SCC 303; Prabatbhai Aahir Alias Prabatbhai Bhimsinghbhai Karmur and others vs. State of Gujarat and Another : (2017) 9 SCC 641; Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab : (2014) 6 SCC 466 and B.S.Joshi and Other vs. State of Haryana and Another : (2003)4 SCC 67.
